posts.author: SGHarlekin
posts.body:
I've recently experienced a lot of crashes using MV and I think I tracked the issue down to me having expanded my list of skills to 1.000. That and perhaps the ever growing amount of data cotnained in the project seem to have lead to frequent crashing.
I was surprised to say the least, having used the engine for 8.000+ hours without a single issue. When tracking the resoucres used by the engine, MV never used more than 400MB of ram and like 1% of my CPU, so I was sure that would be no problem. However, when asking around on a discord server,
@AceOfAces_Mod
brought this little
4GB Patch tool
to my attention.
This very little tool patches x86 executables in order to let them have 4GB (instead of only 2) of virtual memory on x64 platforms.
Now I don't know how or why, but it seemed to have completely fixed the crashing for the time being. (Of course there is also a chance that windows' code being now written to 40% by AI has also something to do with this, but I digress)
In any case, I wanted to share this information with my fellow RMers.

After some more usage, it looks like Windows 11, version 25H2 seems to be the culprit for me. Ever since that update, it looks like both MV and MZ are leaking memory. It's not really an issue with the patch. You can open your task manager and scroll through your animations tab or other tabs and maps and see the ram usage rise. This is generally normal. The problem is that the ram is never being released again after you close the tabs or maps as it normally would, resulting in the crash inevitably happening. The patch merely gives it access to more ram, resulting in a crash at a later moment.
I don't have high hopes for a fix any time soon, considering how microsoft has been handling their OS in recent years. I'm considering going back to win10 whenever I do my next cleanup. Right now I just have task manager running whenever I develop and once RM gets close to 2GB of ram usage, I just restart it.

Update on the specific issue of having the engine crash within the hour despite the 4GB patch (and not touching 4000MB of RAM from what I could remember. If it was, it was happening way too rapidly to be normal.)
Frustrated, I hadn't touched my project in a couple months, so I'm not sure if some sort of update resolved the issue during my break, or me attempting the following had.
I'm not sure why or how, but one of the following seemed to have been exacerbating the problem and causing the engine to crash way before it should have. I saw this suggested somewhere, and it worked for me. I went ahead and turned all of the following off. I did not bother trying to pinpoint which one was the offender, but it seemed to be one or multiple of the following:
- Steam Overlay
- Steam Cloud (Global)
- Xbox Overlay
- Discord Overlay
- Nvidia Overlay
I stress tested the engine and got it to 2100MB without crashing, so the patch seems to be working again.
I am now back to being able to put hours of work into the engine once more. It will no longer crash within 30 minutes.
I started working on my project again last night after the stress test without closing the engine. For two hours it stayed at around 1600MB (closing the playtest dropped it from 2100MB ).
Right now, after opening the engine again, I am at 3 hours of work. The highest RAM I've seen so far is 600MB.
